use_case: TaraHome blog cover for a homeowner guide to Home Assistant user and guest access
prompt: Create a clean, photorealistic editorial smart-home photograph for a TaraHome blog article about giving family members or guests limited smart-home control. Landscape 3:2 composition, designed to remain clear when center-cropped to both 16:9 and 16:10. Show a warm, real residential entry and adjacent living room with cream plaster walls, a natural oak console, soft late-morning window light, and restrained dark-forest-green accents. An ordinary adult homeowner and an older child or visiting adult stand naturally beside a permanently mounted slim wall tablet and a normal physical light switch. The homeowner calmly shows the other person the shared household control point; the interaction feels practical, trusted, and everyday. Keep the tablet screen dim and abstract with no readable interface, words, icons, logos, or app imitation. Include a softly lit table lamp so the smart-home purpose reads without futuristic hardware. Use premium but candid residential editorial photography, realistic anatomy and hands, believable materials and lighting, subtle lived-in texture, and a mid-distance eye-level 35mm-lens feel. Keep both people, the wall tablet, physical switch, and lamp inside the central crop-safe area. No embedded headline, title, lettering, numbers, labels, logos, watermark, fake app screen, readable UI, charts, graphs, diagrams, arrows, decorative routing/network/path lines, translucent panels, inset frames, floating UI cards, progress bars, glowing effects, badges, split-screen layout, exaggerated locks, surveillance imagery, server racks, invented futuristic devices, generic AI-tech symbolism, extra people, or duplicate devices.
